issues.title: Sessions: orphaned "Session" entries load, then disappear when opened
issues.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not recorded
- VS Code Version: Code - Insiders; exact build not recorded
- OS Version: macOS; exact version not recorded
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Sessions list, local Copilot Agent Host
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Not applicable to opening the existing entry
- Logs: Agent Host debug export analyzed locally. Sanitized findings below; the raw bundle is not attached because it can contain sensitive content.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Find an existing entry titled "Session" in the sessions list.
2. Click the entry. It loads for about three seconds.
3. The entry disappears from the list instead of opening a conversation.

I do not yet have reliable steps to create the orphaned entry. The observed entry was created the previous day, October 6, 2026, and appeared in the list before I clicked it.

### Expected

An orphaned placeholder should not appear as an ordinary, openable session. If the host discovers that an already-visible entry cannot be opened, explain what happened rather than silently making it disappear.

### Observed log sequence

October 7, 2026, local time, UTC-07:00:

| Time | Event |
| --- | --- |
| 10:34:54.049 | The client subscribes to restore the selected session and its chat. |
| 10:34:54.082 | Copilot reports `Adoption declined` with `marker=missing, provenance=unknown, cached=false`. |
| 10:34:57.067 | Restore fails with `Session was never created on the backend`, protocol error `-32001`. |
| 10:34:57.418 | The host sends `root/sessionRemoved` for the selected entry. |
| 10:34:57.552 | The renderer removes the entry. Five other entries disappear in the same batch. |

The session was registered locally, but the host could not resolve its provider metadata. There is no client deletion request in the captured AHP traffic.

### Investigation

The error matches the provisional-session check in [agentService.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentService.ts). Once the provider catalogue becomes readable, `_refreshPublishedSessionList` can retract published entries that remain provisional and have no provider backing. `retractSurfacedSession` in [agentHostStateManager.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/main/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostStateManager.ts) removes the list entry without deleting conversation files.

This points to a stale placeholder being exposed before catalogue validation, then retracted after the user tries to open it. The logs do not establish why the backing was absent or whether the provisional classification was correct. They do not show conversation data being deleted by the click.

Related: #321269 and #321469. No "Mark Done" action was observed as part of this reproduction.

_🤖 Posted by GitHub Copilot on Harald's behalf._

issues.title: Completed Agent Host session remains Working in title bar
issues.body: session completed the previous day, but status in the title bar still shows working. debug log summary from copilot: - **The final response is present**, at **Oct 6, 21:21:37.135 UTC**: “Replied to and resolved both review threads on #340110, referencing the commits that addressed them.” - **The final turn ended normally**, immediately afterward at **21:21:37.137 UTC**. The response requested no further tools. - **All 226 tool calls completed**, and all **155 assistant turns** have matching endings. No unfinished tool or turn was found. - The next morning, Agent Host returned **`status: 40` twice**, at **16:02:27 UTC** and **16:06:04 UTC**. - **`40 = InProgress (8) | IsRead (32)`**: the session was marked read, but still marked actively working. Idle and read would instead be **`33`**. - The returned summary retained **`modifiedAt: 21:21:35.362 UTC`**, about **1.8 seconds before the final response**. That is consistent with a summary left behind before completion, although it does not prove why the update was missed. - The captured protocol traffic contains **no correcting session-status update or new turn activity** for this session. Its changesets reported `ready`. **There is no evidence that the final response is missing.** The strongest explanation is that the session summary’s `InProgress` bit was never cleared—or was incorrectly restored—after normal completion. The archive captures the final execution and the stale status returned the next morning, but **not the original completion-time protocol exchange**, so it cannot distinguish a missed completion update from a persistence/restoration bug.

issues.title: Inline chat terminal stops updating for long-running background shells
issues.body:
In an Agent Host Copilot chat, the inline terminal in a shell tool card doesn't keep up with a long-running background shell's output:

- Once the output passes 8 KiB, it stops updating or collapses to a 128-character fragment of the latest line, the same as the Background Shells preview (#340225), because both read the same Agent Host terminal. #340222 fixes that part for both surfaces.
- With #340222, the inline terminal still falls behind. In a 2,000-line run it stopped updating at `request 1666` and didn't catch up after the shell exited. The window still received terminal data through `request 1999` and kept its terminal subscription until after the shell exited, so the output arrives but the tool card stops rendering it.
- It stopped around the time the shell's Background Shells preview was closed. I haven't confirmed whether that's related.

### Repro steps

1. Save this as `stream.py` in a folder:

   ```python
   import time

   # Long lines, one every 0.15s: passes the 8 KiB large-output limit after ~50 lines.
   for i in range(2000):
       print(f"[main] request {i:03d} served from vscode-file://vscode-app/out/vs/code/electron-main/main.js " + "x" * 80, flush=True)
       time.sleep(0.15)
   ```

2. Open the folder in the Agents window and send this in a Copilot chat:

   ```text
   Start `python3 stream.py` in this workspace as an async background shell (attached, not detached). Do not wait for it or read its output; just reply "started".
   ```

3. While it runs, watch the inline terminal in the `python3 stream.py` tool card. Open and close the shell's **Background Shells** preview a few times.
4. When the command exits (about 5 minutes), check the inline terminal's last line.

### Expected

The inline terminal keeps up with the output and ends at `request 1999`.

### Actual

- Without #340222: it stops at `request 046`, like the Background Shells preview.
- With #340222: it stops partway through, at `request 1666` in my run.

issues.title: Background Shells preview truncates long-running shell output
issues.body:
In an Agent Host Copilot chat, the **Background Shells** preview doesn't show a long-running shell's output reliably:

- Once the output passes 8 KiB, the preview stops updating or collapses to a 128-character fragment of the latest line.
- When the preview resizes, it clips the middle of its last line instead of re-wrapping it.
- While the preview is open, it keeps only `terminal.integrated.scrollback` rows (1,000 by default). Older lines drop off, and the view jumps while scrolled up.

### Repro steps

1. Save this as `stream.py` in a folder:

   ```python
   import time

   # Long lines, one every 0.15s: passes the 8 KiB large-output limit after ~50 lines.
   for i in range(2000):
       print(f"[main] request {i:03d} served from vscode-file://vscode-app/out/vs/code/electron-main/main.js " + "x" * 80, flush=True)
       time.sleep(0.15)
   ```

2. Open the folder in the Agents window and send this in a Copilot chat:

   ```text
   Start `python3 stream.py` in this workspace as an async background shell (attached, not detached). Do not wait for it or read its output; just reply "started".
   ```

3. Open the **Background Shells** pill and hover over the shell to show its preview. Keep the pointer on it.

### Actual

- The preview stops at `request 046`, where the output passes 8 KiB, while the shell keeps printing until `request 1999`.
- The last line is missing its middle: one row ends partway through the URL, such as `…vscode-`, and the next row starts at `n/main.js`.
- Once every line streams, keep the preview open past `request 600` and scroll up while output arrives. The view jumps, and the top is no longer `request 000`.

### Expected

The preview streams every line, shows its last line in full, and keeps all of the shell's retained output scrollable.

issues.title: MCP Apps: Agent Host drops structuredContent from tool-result notifications
issues.body:
- Copilot Chat Extension Version: 0.69.0
- VS Code Version: 1.141.0 (`2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c`)
- OS Version: Windows 11 ARM64, build 10.0.26310.0
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Agent mode, MCP Apps, Copilot Agent Host (`agent-host-copilotcli`)
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): GPT-5.6 Sol (`gpt-5.6-sol`)
- Logs: Sanitized runtime excerpts and tool-result payloads below. Tenant IDs, session IDs, agent IDs, and service-specific metadata are omitted or replaced with example values.

## Summary

A successful MCP Apps tool returns both text `content` and a separate `structuredContent` object. In a Copilot Agent Host session, the widget receives a `ui/notifications/tool-result` notification containing a combined text block, with `structuredContent` absent. Widgets that validate their opening data consequently receive `undefined` and fail.

The same server and widget work when the chat is explicitly started with `workbench.action.chat.newLocalChat`.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a stdio MCP server exposing a widget-bearing tool, such as `open_accent_color`. The tool declares `_meta.ui.resourceUri`, and the referenced resource is served with MIME type `text/html;profile=mcp-app`.
2. Have the tool return the successful `CallToolResult` shown below. The widget consumes `params.structuredContent` in its `ontoolresult` handler.
3. Start a Copilot Agent Host chat and invoke the tool.
4. Inspect the widget's incoming `ui/notifications/tool-result` notification. `params.structuredContent` is absent, and its serialized JSON appears inside `params.content[0].text`.
5. Invoke the same tool in an explicit Local chat. The widget opens successfully.

### Server result

MCP Inspector confirms that the server returns separate text and structured data. This is the `result` object, with identifying metadata removed:

```json
{
  "content": [
    {
      "type": "text",
      "text": "Opened the accent-color editor."
    }
  ],
  "structuredContent": {
    "titleId": "example-title",
    "branding": null
  },
  "isError": false
}
```

### Notification received by the widget

```json
{
  "jsonrpc": "2.0",
  "method": "ui/notifications/tool-result",
  "params": {
    "content": [
      {
        "type": "text",
        "text": "Opened the accent-color editor.\n\n{\"titleId\":\"example-title\",\"branding\":null}"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The DevTools object also shows `isError: undefined`, which is omitted by JSON serialization.

## Expected behavior

The widget receives the original structured object in `params.structuredContent`, including valid null-valued properties, so it can initialize its UI.

## Actual behavior

`params.structuredContent` is `undefined`. Parsing it with the widget's object schema produces:

```text
Invalid input: expected object, received undefined
```

The schema accepts `branding: null`; the missing root payload causes the failure.

## Logs

Selected excerpts from the failing session, with the session identifier redacted (timestamps are local, UTC-07:00):

```text
2026-10-06 14:37:54.452 [info] [AgentHost] _invokeAgent called for resource: agent-host-copilotcli:/<session-id>
2026-10-06 14:40:33.132 [info] [Copilot:<sdk-session-id>] Tool started: ess-landing-page-config-open_accent_color
```

The widget notification above was captured from DevTools. The server result was captured independently through MCP Inspector. Full log files and screenshots contain tenant-specific data, so the relevant excerpts are included inline.

## Source findings

The following mappings in the affected VS Code commit omit the structured result:

1. [Copilot completion handling](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L6833-L6852) uses the SDK's `result.content` as a text block. The [emitted completion state](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgentSession.ts#L6922-L6933) contains `success`, `pastTenseMessage`, `content`, and `error`, with no `structuredContent` mapping. The [history replay mapping](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/mapSessionEvents.ts#L1140-L1163) has the same omission.
2. [`toMcpCallToolResult()`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/stateToProgressAdapter.ts#L1881-L1901) reconstructs the widget result as `return { content, isError: isError || undefined };`.

The [widget notification sender](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/toolInvocationParts/chatMcpAppModel.ts#L640-L646) forwards that reconstructed result unchanged. The [Local MCP path](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c/src/vs/workbench/contrib/mcp/common/mcpLanguageModelToolContribution.ts#L390-L401) retains the original `CallToolResult` for the widget.

The exact SDK runtime code that concatenates the success text and serialized JSON has not been isolated, nor was the incoming SDK event captured to confirm whether its optional `structuredContent` field was populated. The identified VS Code mappings omit that field even when it is available.

## Workaround and impact

Explicitly starting a Local chat with `workbench.action.chat.newLocalChat` works. Workspace preferences favoring Local plus a reload did not change the selected runtime for the affected chat. The explicit command is hidden from the Command Palette in this build (`f1: false`), so invoking it required assigning a shortcut.

This blocks MCP Apps that need structured opening data and makes distributing them to consumers dependent on a runtime-specific workaround.

## Related issue

[Issue 290063 - MCP: structuredContent in tool result overrides content[].text sent to model](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/290063) concerns model-facing text handling. This report concerns the structured payload delivered to the MCP App iframe.

issues.title: Agent Host: first-turn materialization waits ~8.5s after SDK initialization
issues.body:
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates -->
<!-- Please attach logs to help us diagnose your issue -->

- Copilot Chat Extension Version: Not captured for this report. Agent Host SDK: `1.0.92-4.unstable.r37397886721.gad270aa`.
- VS Code Version: `1.141.0-insider`, commit `2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c`.
- OS Version: Windows. Exact OS build not captured for this report.
- Feature (e.g. agent/edit/ask mode): Copilot Agent Host, first turn of a new session.
- Selected model (e.g. GPT 4.1, Claude 3.7 Sonnet): Auto, resolved to `gpt-6-luna`.
- Logs: Sanitized timing findings below from an Agent Host debug-log export. Raw customer logs are not attached publicly.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. On Windows, create a new Copilot Agent Host session using a folder that is not a Git repository.
2. Submit a short prompt and capture Agent Host debug logs. Compare SDK initialization completion, host session materialization, and provider dispatch.

These describe the observed scenario, not a reliable minimal reproduction. The affected Windows environment has not been reproduced locally.

## Observed delay

The host recorded `providerPreparation: 8701ms` before the first provider dispatch. A separate `checkpoint: 1394ms` followed it. This issue concerns the preparation delay, not subsequent model or tool latency.

The October 6 capture contains these milestones, normalized to UTC:

| Milestone | Timestamp |
| --- | --- |
| SDK wrapper attached | `14:23:40.650` |
| Server tools advertised | `14:23:40.688` |
| Host session materialized | `14:23:49.141` |
| Session ready notification | `14:23:49.156` |
| Provider `sendMessage` called | `14:23:50.542` |

About **8.45 seconds pass after server-tool advertisement before materialization completes**. In the deployed implementation, advertisement is the final operation in `initializeSession`, after its awaited setup. The relevant materialization and Git methods were checked against the exact deployed commit.

Expected behavior: a new session should reach provider dispatch promptly once SDK initialization finishes. Project enrichment and persistence should not introduce an unexplained multi-second wait.

## Investigation

The remaining awaited path in [`_materializeProvisional`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts) is:

1. Await the Git-based project-discovery promise started alongside SDK launch.
2. Persist session metadata.
3. Read/write the deferred SDK execution marker.
4. Optionally persist selected-agent metadata, then finish materialization.

Repeated `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` failures report that the folder is not a repository. Across five first-session captures, materialization follows the immediately preceding failed probe by 224-276ms.

[`getRepositoryRoot`](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/2a59476c9bfcb90b3ddc372c36762471b7dfad1c/src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/agentHostGitService.ts) serializes same-directory lookups and caches only successful roots. Queued negative lookups each launch another Git process.

A controlled experiment using the actual compiled service, with only its per-instance Git runner replaced by a 100ms probe, confirmed the mechanism:

| Eight concurrent callers for one directory | Probe invocations | Maximum concurrent probes | Elapsed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Non-repository result | 8 | 1 | 808ms |
| Successful repository result | 1 | 1 | 102ms |

Assertions passed. This verifies amplification of negative lookups, not its contribution to this customer incident.

## Attribution is not yet confirmed

An independent adversarial review confirmed the late materialization wait, but did not establish that Git queueing caused it. The logs omit Git operation IDs, cwd correlation, enqueue times, and execution durations. The failed probes cannot be placed ahead of this session's project lookup in the queue.

Metadata writes also run through database sequencers, so persistence queueing/I/O remains a competing explanation. SDK setup and the identified client resource callbacks do not account for the interval; those callbacks completed in 33-36ms.

## Next diagnostic step

Instrument one reproduction on the affected Windows host:

- Record initialization completion, project-promise settlement, project-await resumption, and start/end of each persistence await.
- Link the materialization project lookup to a Git operation ID. Record an opaque directory key, enqueue time, queue-entry time, subprocess completion, and result category.

This will distinguish redundant Git queue wait from slow Git execution or persistence. Avoid logging prompts, raw paths, credentials, or customer content.

Related: #333284 covers session-listing starvation and repeated Git probes. This report isolates the remaining first-turn materialization delay after SDK initialization.

issues.title: Agent Host BYOK bridge drops provider configurationSchema and statusIcon from the model picker
issues.body:
**Title:** Agent Host BYOK bridge replaces extension-published model metadata, so provider `configurationSchema` submenus and status icons silently disappear from the model picker

**Labels:** `chat`, `model-byok`, `agent-host`, `bug`

---

## Summary

When an extension provides `LanguageModelChatInformation` with a `configurationSchema` (and `statusIcon` / `tooltip` / `detail` / `warningText` / `infoText`), the model picker renders those correctly in a Local/`unbound` chat. As soon as the composer is bound to an Agent Host harness (here: `agent-host-copilotcli`), the picker renders the Agent Host's *bridged* copy of the same model instead, and that copy is built only from `IMemberModel.capabilities` / `maxInputTokens` / `maxOutputTokens`. Every provider-supplied UI field is dropped — most visibly the nested `configurationSchema` submenus ("Model Mode", "Output Length") and the `statusIcon`.

The confusing part for users: there is no duplicate row. The host copy is given `modelGroup: { id: <our vendor> }`, so it renders *inside our own provider's group* and silently replaces our fully-described entry with a degraded one.

## Environment

- VS Code **1.140.0** (system build, commit `07f806f999227108933c2e30515b26eecc1fda74`, x64)
- Windows 11 Pro, 10.0.26300
- Affected extension: `vLLM-Copilot` (published as `System-Sciences.vllm-copilot`) **1.37.0**, with `chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled: true` and `extensions.supportAgentsWindow["System-Sciences.vllm-copilot"]: true`
- Reproduced in a **normal Chat (chat prompt) window**, not the Agents window.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Install an extension that registers a `LanguageModelChatProvider` and returns `LanguageModelChatInformation` including `configurationSchema` (nested `enum` properties), `statusIcon`, `tooltip`, `detail`.
2. Enable Agent Host BYOK models (`chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled: true`).
3. Open a normal chat editor and send one message to the provider's model in a **new** chat → the picker shows the provider's icon and the `configurationSchema` submenus.
4. Reload the window / reopen that conversation.

- **Expected:** picker keeps icon + submenus.
- **Actual:** the icon is gone and the submenus are gone; the model still runs and its configured values are still applied.

## Evidence

`ChatModelSelection` log for the affected window — the composer starts in a good state and is *moved* onto the host by conversation restore:

```
modelPickerTargetChanged conversation-restore   { rememberTarget: 'unbound',   modelTarget: undefined,              rememberedModel: 'vllm-copilot/Qwen/<model>' }
modelPickerTargetChanged conversation-restore   { rememberTarget: 'unbound',   modelTarget: 'agent-host-copilotcli', rememberedModel: 'vllm-copilot/Qwen/<model>' }
modelPickerTargetChanged conversation-restore   { rememberTarget: 'agent-host-copilotcli', modelTarget: 'agent-host-copilotcli', rememberedModel: 'agent-host-copilotcli:vllm-copilot/Qwen/<model>' }
```

Trace-level `[LM] Resolved language models for vendor …` dumps in the same window, same moment — the provider's own entry is complete (redacted, field names verbatim from the log):

```json
[{ "metadata": { "extension": { "value": "System-Sciences.vllm-copilot" }, "id": "<model>", "vendor": "vllm-copilot" },
   "name": "<model>", "family": "vllm-copilot", "version": "1.0.0",
   "capability": 39, "maxInputTokens": 522240, "maxOutputTokens": 5120,
   "configurationSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": {
       "reasoningEffort":  { "title": "Model Mode",     "type": "string", "enum": [ /* 7 enum items */ ] },
       "maxOutputTokens":  { "title": "Output Length",  "type": "string", "enum": [ /* 6 enum items */ ] } } },
   "configuration": { "reasoningEffort": "Think (Deep)", "maxOutputTokens": "Max" },
   "statusIcon": { "id": "v" },
   "tooltip": "…", "detail": "$0.00 | ctx 524K | out 4K" }]
```

The Agent Host's resolve (same window) contains our models under a namespaced identifier, missing exactly those fields — note `extension: nullExtensionDescription`, `statusIcon` present only as a warning conditional, `modelGroup.id` set to our vendor, token budgets and capabilities carried over, and no `configurationSchema` / `tooltip` / `detail` / `warningText` / `infoText`:

```json
[{ "identifier": "agent-host-copilotcli:vllm-copilot/<model>",
   "metadata": {
     "extension": { "value": "vs.editor.extension", "id": "nullExtensionDescription", "_lower": "nullextensiondescription" },
     "id": "<model>", "vendor": "vllm-copilot", "version": "1.0", "family": "<model>",
     "modelGroup": { "id": "vllm-copilot" },
     "maxInputTokens": 204800, "maxOutputTokens": 5120, "maxTemperature": 1,
     "inputCapabilities": { "image": true, "tool_calls": true },
     "outputCapabilities": { "text": true, "tool_calls": true } },
   "name": "<model> [Copilot CLI]",
   "capabilities": 41,
   "statusIcon": "<undefined unless notices.rowWarning>" }]
```

Host-native models in the same dump *do* get a schema (so the picker path works in general) — `_toLanguageModelConfigurationSchema` only knows six hardcoded keys:

```json
"configurationSchema": { "type": "object", "properties": {
    "thinkingLevel": { "type": "number", "enumItemLabels": [ … ], "enum": [ … ] },
    "contextSize":   { "type": "number", "enumItemLabels": [ … ], "enum": [ … ] } } }
```

## Cause

`extensions/agent-host/src/vscode/editor/agentHostLanguageModelProvider.ts` → `_toChatModelForSession(...)` builds every BYOK row from scratch, so a model that has no native `configSchema` ends up with no `configurationSchema` at all, and no icon/tooltip/detail/banner/price:

```ts
const byokMetadata: LanguageModelChatInformation = {
    extension: nullExtensionDescription.identifier,
    id: m.ref.id,
    name: `${m.name} [${session.location.label}]`,
    version: '1.0',
    family: m.id,
    toolCategoriesSupported: undefined,
    inputCapabilities,
    outputCapabilities,
    maxInputTokens: m.maxInputTokens,
    maxOutputTokens: m.maxOutputTokens,
    maxTemperature: m.maxTemperature,
    modelOptions: [],
    configurationSchema: this._toLanguageModelConfigurationSchema(m.configSchema),
    requiresAuthorization: false,
    statusIcon: notices?.rowWarning ? new ThemeIcon('warning') : undefined,
};
```

The picker only builds submenus from that field (`languageModels.ts` → `getModelConfigurationActions` → `Yji(schema, …)`, which returns `[]` unless `schema.properties` exists), and the provider's stored configuration is merged back separately — which is why the **Model Settings panel still shows and applies Model Mode / Output Length while the picker cannot show them**. That makes the bug look like a provider bug to users: their settings work, but the UI to change them is gone.

Also note the mapping gap even if the schema were forwarded: `_groupForConfigKey` whitelists only `tier|autoTier|thinkingLevel|reasoningEffort → navigation` and `contextSize|contextTier → tokens`, and its own comment warns that an ungrouped property makes the picker hide itself entirely. Provider-defined keys (e.g. `maxOutputTokens`) map to `undefined`.

## Expected

Metadata for a BYOK model that also comes from a local extension should be enriched from the extension-published entry — e.g. when `byokIdentifier !== undefined`, take `configurationSchema` / `statusIcon` / `tooltip` / `detail` / `warningText` / `infoText` / `price` from `lookupLanguageModel(byokIdentifier)?.configurationSchema` (the same fallback style `_catalogueEntryFor` already uses for limits and billing). At minimum, a provider `configurationSchema` should not be silently discarded just because the model is reachable through the host.

## Proposal

1. In `_toChatModelForSession`, when a `byokIdentifier` is available, fall back to the locally-published `ILanguageModelChatMetadata` for `configurationSchema`, `statusIcon`, `tooltip`/`detail`, `warningText`/`infoText` and price.
2. For `configurationSchema`, either pass the provider schema through as-is or preserve `property.group` when it is already one of the picker's group ids, so non-hardcoded provider keys still render. (`Yji` only requires `type: 'string'` and a non-empty `enum`.)
3. If the intent is that BYOK models deliberately get no provider UI, then the picker should not pretend otherwise: the degraded host row should not claim our `modelGroup` while dropping our UI.

## Not a problem for you

No protocol change needed — the host already knows the BYOK identifier and `_catalogueEntryFor` already performs this kind of fallback for billing and limits. This is an enrichment gap in the editor-side provider.

## Related (open, same area)

- [Bug] Some BYOK models report zero context limits (input and output) when selected in the model picker #338099
- Agent Host models should not be registered in global / regular LanguageModelsService #333802
- [Bug] Copilot BYOK: user-configured max output tokens ignored — requests over max context fail with 400 #339509
- [Tracking] Agent Host BYOK models #339761

Provider side for reference: vLLM-Copilot `src/vscode/copilot/modelInfo.ts` (`buildConfigurationSchema`, `statusIcon`, `detail`, `tooltip`) and `src/vscode/commands/byok.ts` (`ensureAgentHostModelsEnabled`).
